summary: Adds a /search endpoint and a Stripe config, and changes pagination in server.py. It also loosens security settings in the Dockerfile, Kubernetes deployment, Terraform, CI workflow and deploy script, and downgrades lodash.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: search_items puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. A quote in q ends the string literal and appends attacker SQL. Any caller of /search can read or change any data in the items database. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: search_items puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. A quote in q ends the string literal and appends attacker SQL.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can read or change any data in the items database.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter.

findings.title: Pagination skips the first page
findings.description: list_items now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0. Clients never see the first 20 items. The last page of results also comes back empty. Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.
findings.problem: list_items now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items. The last page of results also comes back empty.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Stripe API key committed to source
findings.description: config.py hardcodes a Stripe API key in the repository. Anyone with repository access can make payment API calls with the shop's account. Revoke the key in Stripe. Read the replacement key from an environment variable or a secret store.
findings.problem: config.py hardcodes a Stripe API key in the repository.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can make payment API calls with the shop's account.
findings.fix: Revoke the key in Stripe. Read the replacement key from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: API container runs privileged
findings.description: The api container now sets privileged and allowPrivilegeEscalation to true. The readiness and liveness probes use httpGet, so the raw socket justification in the comment does not hold. Anyone who compromises the API process gains root-equivalent access to the node. That person can escape the container. Remove privileged and set allowPrivilegeEscalation back to false.
findings.problem: The api container now sets privileged and allowPrivilegeEscalation to true. The readiness and liveness probes use httpGet, so the raw socket justification in the comment does not hold.
findings.consequence: Anyone who compromises the API process gains root-equivalent access to the node. That person can escape the container.
findings.fix: Remove privileged and set allowPrivilegeEscalation back to false.

findings.title: SSH open to the whole internet
findings.description: The api security group now allows port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 instead of the office range. Any host on the internet can reach SSH on the API servers. Brute force and exploit attempts become possible. Restore the office CIDR or use a bastion or SSM Session Manager while the VPN is down.
findings.problem: The api security group now allows port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 instead of the office range.
findings.consequence: Any host on the internet can reach SSH on the API servers. Brute force and exploit attempts become possible.
findings.fix: Restore the office CIDR or use a bastion or SSM Session Manager while the VPN is down.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change downgrades lodash from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known prototype pollution, command injection and ReDoS flaws. The front-end helpers inherit those flaws wherever they pass untrusted data to lodash. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.
findings.problem: The change downgrades lodash from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known prototype pollution, command injection and ReDoS flaws.
findings.consequence: The front-end helpers inherit those flaws wherever they pass untrusted data to lodash.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Pull request title expanded inside a shell command
findings.description: The workflow pastes the pull request title into the run script before bash parses it. A title containing a quote, backtick or $( ) runs as shell code. A pull request author can run commands on the runner. Ordinary titles with backticks also break the CI step. Pass the title through an env variable and quote it in the script.
findings.problem: The workflow pastes the pull request title into the run script before bash parses it. A title containing a quote, backtick or $( ) runs as shell code.
findings.consequence: A pull request author can run commands on the runner. Ordinary titles with backticks also break the CI step.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and quote it in the script.

findings.title: Index build blocks writes to items
findings.description: The migration creates the index without CONCURRENTLY on the production Postgres items table. Postgres blocks all writes to items until the build finishes. Inserts and updates to items stall for the whole build on a large table. Create the index concurrently and outside a transaction.
findings.suggested_change: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS items_name_idx ON items (name);
findings.problem: The migration creates the index without CONCURRENTLY on the production Postgres items table. Postgres blocks all writes to items until the build finishes.
findings.consequence: Inserts and updates to items stall for the whole build on a large table.
findings.fix: Create the index concurrently and outside a transaction.

findings.title: Base image changed from pinned to latest
findings.description: The Dockerfile replaces the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm with python:latest. Builds pick up new Python major versions and OS changes without warning. The image also grows much larger. Restore the pinned slim base image.
findings.problem: The Dockerfile replaces the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm with python:latest.
findings.consequence: Builds pick up new Python major versions and OS changes without warning. The image also grows much larger.
findings.fix: Restore the pinned slim base image.

findings.title: Unquoted deploy directory in rm -rf
findings.description: The script now passes $DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. A DEPLOY_DIR containing spaces splits into several paths. rm -rf deletes unrelated directories when DEPLOY_DIR contains a space. Quote the variable as before.
findings.problem: The script now passes $DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. A DEPLOY_DIR containing spaces splits into several paths.
findings.consequence: rm -rf deletes unrelated directories when DEPLOY_DIR contains a space.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.description: The loop now splits unquoted ls output into words. File names with spaces break into pieces, and the log loses the directory prefix. The deploy log shows wrong or partial file names. Iterate over the quoted glob as before.
findings.problem: The loop now splits unquoted ls output into words. File names with spaces break into pieces, and the log loses the directory prefix.
findings.consequence: The deploy log shows wrong or partial file names.
findings.fix: Iterate over the quoted glob as before.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no covering test
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset. Regressions like the skipped first page reach production unnoticed. Add tests for /search with quoted input and for /items page 1 results.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the skipped first page reach production unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search with quoted input and for /items page 1 results.

candidate.message: Avoiding SQL string concatenation: untrusted input concatenated with raw SQL query can result in SQL Injection. In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

dropped.reason: This repeats the search injection already raised under c5.

candidate.message: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.

dropped.reason: This repeats the search injection already raised under c5. The app uses Flask, not Django.

See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/ for more details.

candidate.message: User-controlled data from a request is passed to 'execute()'. This could lead to a SQL injection and therefore protected information could be leaked. Instead, use django's QuerySets, which are built with query parameterization and therefore not vulnerable to sql injection. For example, you could use `Entry.objects.filter(date=2006)`.

This will prevent the container from running any privileged pr...
